title: Safe Power-Up Sequencer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robot Safety
description: Put the seven shuffled steps of the safe power-up sequence into the order you would do them, commit once, then read why each step sits where it does. Used in Chapter 3.

educational.topic: The safe power-up sequence for a robot arm
learningObjectives: Implement the safe power-up sequence by arranging seven shuffled steps in the correct order, with at least 6 of the 7 steps in their correct positions on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Perform the procedure by ordering its steps, commit the whole arrangement once, then compare it with the correct order and the reason for each position
keyQuestions: Which steps must be finished before the supply is switched on?
Why does the simulation come before any power?
Why is the first move small and slow?
commonMisconceptions: The E-stop can be reached for later
assessmentOpportunities: One committed arrangement of seven steps; 6 of 7 in the correct position on the first Check for mastery

controls.label: Click a step to select it
Step
values: the seven steps, in their current order
